Hi Sanjay — thanks for the note and the PO. Looping in Marissa (tax) and Ben (billing/collections).

Short answer up front: if PayFlux BV is a VAT-registered B2B purchaser and the supply is made to a business establishment in the EU, we typically issue net invoices with reverse-charge (i.e., no VAT charged by Redwood) provided we validate your VAT registration and EU entity details. If PayFlux is not VAT-registered or the buyer is a consumer, standard VAT would apply.

What we need to proceed:
- VAT ID (official registration number) and a scanned certificate of VAT registration (national document or VIES extract).
- Confirm legal invoicing entity (company name + registered address).
- Clarify whether the billed entity is the same as the entity that will make payment (AR email).

Proposed routing options:
1) Reverse-charge (preferred for B2B EU entities): once we validate the VAT ID we will reissue invoices net and mark them as reverse-charge, with the appropriate place-of-supply notes on the invoice. Collections can then proceed to release payment without VAT.
2) Interim hold + validation: if validation cannot be completed before your payment run, we can hold VAT on a suspense ledger and reconcile after validation — Collections will not release until we confirm.
3) Self-billing / marketplace flow: if PayFlux prefers self-billing, we can discuss a short agreement (DocuSign) and map to your AP system.

I've attached a quick mapping that shows how we treat platform fees vs. pass-through credits — in most cases both follow the same place-of-supply logic but pass-through cloud credits may be VAT-exempt depending on the contractual flow. See attached workbook for the baseline mapping.

Attachment: proposed-vat-routing.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Action items for Sanjay: please send VAT ID + certificate and confirm AR contact. Ben — can you pause any VAT collection actions until we validate? Marissa — please advise if you need anything else for evidence.

Thanks,
